profile.org_note: The Q3 2026 10-Q says Meritage has twelve homebuilding operating segments (one per state) rolled up into three reportable segments, West, Central and East, reviewed by CEO Phillippe Lord as chief operating decision maker; internally, region or area presidents (for example a Texas region, a Florida region and an Arizona area) run groups of the 23 division offices, but the company names none of them in filings or releases. Land deals start with division land VPs, who prepare a corporate approval package, and every deal goes to a corporate land acquisition committee of executive management and key operating leaders; deals above a set size also need Executive Chairman Steven Hilton, and the Board's Asset Management Committee reviews large land, JV and land-banking transactions. There is no named corporate land head or treasurer: CFO Hilla Sferruzza runs finance and capital markets, and the COO seat has been empty since May 2025.
profile.summary: Scottsdale-based public builder of entry-level and first move-up spec homes in 12 states and 25 markets; 15,026 homes closed in 2025. It held 77,625 lots at 31 December 2025 (55,861 owned, 21,764 under purchase or option contracts) and aims for a four-to-five-year supply. Management has said it still targets about 40% of lots off balance sheet against roughly 31% optioned at 30 September 2026 (third quarter 2026 call transcript), so there is stated room for more lot-option and land-bank financing.

gaps: Land and region rows are not fully confirmed: most facts come from SEC filings, the company's investor and consumer sites, its full press-release archive, directories and one HBA board.

Corporate head of land (chief land officer, SVP or VP of land, national land acquisition or land development): not publicly disclosed. No such officer appears in the FY2025 10-K, the 2026 proxy, the management-team page or any company release; the 10-K says only that the corporate management team leads land acquisition decisions through a corporate land acquisition committee whose members are not named.

Division-level land heads (VP of Land Acquisition, VP of Land Development, VP of Entitlements): none named in sources opened. A January 2026 Meritage posting for a Land Acquisition Vice President in Salt Lake City shows the role runs the division's land department, prepares a 'Corporate Approval Package' for each new deal and works to the Division President and the division's Director of Finance; no names are given.

Segment heads for West, Central and East: not publicly disclosed. The company has not named a region president in a release since 2018 and names none in its 10-K, 10-Qs or proxy; the profile's segment leader fields are left empty except Central, where Kyle Davison (Texas Region President from January 2025, archived bio) is the senior named leader.
Regional president for West segment: not publicly disclosed (Arizona has Area President Rebecca Lundberg; a search snippet once named an 'Elliot Jones' as West Region President, not confirmed).

Regional president for East segment: not publicly disclosed. Directory-only leads: Darren Dupree (Florida Region President, The Org, unverified) and Jonathan White (Area President, Alpharetta GA per a search snippet).

Area head for Mountain West (Denver, Colorado Springs, Northern Colorado, Salt Lake City): not publicly disclosed since Darren Dupree's move; the Nashville area head after Austin Woffinden: not publicly disclosed.
Region president for Steve Harding's 'Region President' title: region not public; no source beyond one directory.

Treasurer / head of treasury or capital markets: not publicly disclosed. The CFO signed the June 2026 credit-facility amendment for the borrower and every guarantor, and no treasurer is named in the 10-K, proxy or 8-Ks opened.

Reporting lines below the executive officers: not public. Executive officers are shown reporting to the CEO by inference. Whether region and area presidents report to CEO Phillippe Lord or to EVP Austin Woffinden since the COO left is not stated anywhere opened.

Chief Operating Officer: vacant. Clint Szubinski (EVP and COO) left on 16 May 2025 (Form 8-K filed 2025-05-13) and was named COO of Dream Finders Homes on 2 June 2026 (Jacksonville Daily Record); Meritage has not named a successor.
Dallas Fort Worth and Nashville: successors to Austin Woffinden (Division President DFW 2018-2025, Area President DFW and Nashville 2025) are not named in sources opened.
Staff changes: the 10-K discloses a workforce reduction approved in late 2025 and completed in early 2026, so directory-sourced names (tagged Inferred) carry extra risk of being out of date.
Personal emails and direct phones: not published. No email pattern was found in a public source; only the shared investor and media mailboxes and Emily Tadano's office line are published.
Division presidents: covered by the separate division sweep (meritage-homes.divisions.json); this file adds none beyond the one unconfirmed Southern California listing.
